stem: Chlorine, $\text{Cl}_2$, is a reactive yellow-green gas. It is a strong oxidising agent.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State how $\text{Cl}_2$ is used in water purification.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: Chlorine has the highest first ionisation energy of the Period 3 elements Na to $\text{Cl}$.
parts.text:
Construct an equation for the first ionisation energy of chlorine.

Include state symbols.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain the general increase in the first ionisation energies of the Period 3 elements.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: The halide ions, $\text{X}^-$ (where X = $\text{Cl}$, Br, I), show clear trends in their physical and chemical properties.
parts.text: State and explain the relative thermal stabilities of the hydrogen halides, HX.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.stem:
The halide ions react easily with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.

The main sulfur-containing product of each reaction is shown in the table.

| halide ion | $\text{Cl}^-$ | $\text{Br}^-$ | $\text{I}^-$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| main sulfur-containing product of reaction with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ | $\text{HSO}_4^-$ | $\text{SO}_2$ | $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ |
| oxidation number of sulfur |  |  |  |
parts.text: Complete the table to show the oxidation number of sulfur in each of the sulfur-containing products.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why different sulfur-containing products are produced when each of these halide ions reacts with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem: $\text{Cl}_2$ reacts with aqueous sodium hydroxide in a disproportionation reaction.
parts.text: State what is meant by disproportionation.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction of $\text{Cl}_2$ with cold aqueous sodium hydroxide.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.stem:
Aluminium reacts with chlorine to form aluminium chloride.

Aluminium chloride can exist as the gaseous molecule $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6\text{(g)}$. This molecule contains coordinate bonds.
parts.text: Draw a diagram that clearly shows all the types of bond present in $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6\text{(g)}$.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text:
Describe what you would see when solid aluminium chloride reacts with water.

Name the type of reaction that occurs.

parts.label: (f)(i)
parts.stem:
0.020 mol of element $\mathbf{Z}$ reacts with excess $\text{Cl}_2$ to form 0.020 mol of a liquid chloride.

The liquid chloride has formula $\mathbf{Z}\text{Cl}_n$, where $n$ is an integer.

$\mathbf{Z}\text{Cl}_n$ reacts vigorously with water at room temperature to give an acidic solution and a white solid.

When excess $\text{AgNO}_3\text{(aq)}$ is added to the solution, 11.54 g of $\text{AgCl}\text{(s)}$ forms.
parts.text: Suggest the type of bonding and structure shown by $\mathbf{Z}\text{Cl}_n$.

parts.label: (g)(i)
parts.stem:
Dichloromethane, $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$, is widely used as an organic solvent.

$\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$ can be prepared by reacting $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$ and $\text{Cl}_2$ at room temperature.

The reaction proceeds via several steps, as shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}
parts.text: Give the name of the mechanism of this reaction.

parts.label: (g)(ii)
parts.text: State the essential condition required for the initiation step to take place.

parts.label: (g)(iv)
parts.text: Identify the products of the step labelled propagation 2.

parts.label: (g)(v)
parts.text: Name the type of reaction shown in the final step.

parts.label: (g)(vi)
parts.text: Suggest the identity of another organic molecule that is a product of the reaction of $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$ and $\text{Cl}_2$ under the same conditions.
